attribution: YAN contributions are manufacturer and literature figures. DAP at 21.2% nitrogen gives about 212 mg/L YAN per g/L by stoichiometry. Blended and organic nutrients are less exact: Fermaid O's organic nitrogen measures low by standard YAN assay but performs well above what the assay suggests, and no single conversion factor captures that properly. Treat the organic figures as indicative.

additives.name: Diammonium Phosphate (DAP)
additives.description: Pure inorganic nitrogen: 21.2% N by weight, so 1 g/L contributes about 212 mg/L of yeast assimilable nitrogen.
additives.usageNotes: Cheap and immediately available. Best added in stages rather than all at pitch.
additives.cautions: Ammonium alone does not supply the amino acids, sterols and vitamins yeast also need. A large single dose late in fermentation can drive a heat spike and is largely wasted — yeast lose their nitrogen transporters past about the one-third sugar break.
additives.attribution: scottlabs.com does not resolve and never did — the supplier's domain is scottlab.com, singular. Repointed to the product category section; Scott Laboratories publishes its figures in the annual Fermentation Handbook, which is the document behind these numbers.

additives.name: Fermaid K
additives.description: A blended nutrient: DAP plus inactivated yeast, amino acids, sterols, thiamine and minerals. About 100 mg/L YAN per g/L.
additives.usageNotes: The general-purpose complete nutrient. Typical dose 25 g/hL (0.25 g/L) at the one-third sugar break.
additives.cautions: Contains DAP, so it counts toward any inorganic nitrogen limit you are working to.

additives.name: Fermaid O
additives.description: Fully organic nitrogen from autolysed yeast — no DAP. Measured YAN is modest, around 40 mg/L per g/L, but it supports fermentation as though it delivered several times that, because the nitrogen arrives as amino acids the yeast can use directly.
additives.usageNotes: The nutrient the TOSNA mead protocol is built around: roughly 1 g/L total, split into four equal doses at 24 h, 48 h, 72 h and the one-third sugar break.
additives.cautions: The gap between measured and effective YAN is well documented but not precisely fixed — treat any single conversion figure, including ours, as approximate.

additives.name: Go-Ferm
additives.description: A rehydration nutrient, not a fermentation nutrient. Micronutrients and sterols taken up by dry yeast during the rehydration window, before they meet the must.
additives.usageNotes: Suspend in water at about 43 °C, cool to 40 °C, then rehydrate the yeast in it. Typical rate is 1.25 g Go-Ferm per gram of yeast.
additives.cautions: Must go in the rehydration water, never the must — added directly it does nothing useful.

additives.name: Yeast Hulls
additives.description: Cell wall fragments that adsorb the medium-chain fatty acids which inhibit yeast late in fermentation, and provide sterols and unsaturated fatty acids.
additives.usageNotes: The standard first intervention for a stuck or sluggish fermentation.
additives.cautions: Contributes essentially no nitrogen — pair with a nitrogen source if YAN is the actual problem.

additives.name: Thiamine (Vitamin B1)
additives.description: An essential yeast cofactor. Deficiency causes sluggish fermentation and elevated volatile acidity.
additives.usageNotes: Regulatory limits typically cap additions around 0.6 mg/L. Present in most blended nutrients already.
additives.cautions: Sulphite destroys thiamine, so heavily sulphited musts run short of it.

additives.name: Brewing Yeast Nutrient
additives.description: Zinc-focused nutrient for wort, which is usually nitrogen-sufficient but zinc-deficient after boiling with stainless.
additives.usageNotes: Added in the last few minutes of the boil. Zinc target is around 0.15–0.30 mg/L.
additives.cautions: Wort rarely needs nitrogen — dosing beer with DAP is generally unnecessary and can produce harsh flavours.
